– the failing test (signature + snippet),

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testNestedJDOM()` calls `doTest("nested", DocumentContainer.MODEL_JDOM, "foo;bar; baz ")`. The method `doTest` runs a JXPath expression and asserts its result equals the expected string `"foo;bar; baz "` which has expected leading and trailing spaces preserved.

The current bug report states that when JXPath evaluates XML content with leading or trailing spaces such as `<value> 12324 56</value>`, it returns the string with those spaces trimmed (e.g., `'12324 56'` instead of `' 12324 56'`). This matches the failure observed in the test since `foo;bar; baz ` ends with a space, but JXPath is trimming it internally.

The test indirectly exercises the XML JDOM model handling with JXPath. The relevant class involved in holding the XML model is `DocumentContainer` constructed with a JDOM model type. However, the actual processing of the XML node values to strings occurs via pointer classes such as `NodePointer` and its descendants.

From the snippet of `NodePointer.getValue()`, the method obtains a `valuePointer` (via `getValuePointer()` which calls `getImmediateValuePointer()`) and eventually returns either `valuePointer.getValue()` or the underlying `getNode()` value.

Critically, the default implementation does not trim or alter the string in `NodePointer` itself, rather it just returns `getNode()`. The bug report description strongly implies that somewhere deeper down in the XML node handling or string extraction logic (potentially in a JDOM-specific subclass of `NodePointer` or related logic) automatic trimming of string values is done, either as a side effect or by design.

No recent bug reports appear to be related. The core issue is that JXPath in XML string retrieval automatically trims whitespace from string values, resulting in unexpected loss of leading/trailing spaces when retrieving text from XML elements through the JXPath API.

Hence, the root cause of the bug is an unintended string trimming occurring in the XML node string extraction within the JXPath model implementation, especially for the JDOM model used in the test. This trimming causes the assertion failure in `testNestedJDOM()` since the trailing space is lost.

The fix should be applied to the place that extracts text from XML nodes or creates string values from those nodes inside the JDOM model integration of JXPath.

Next, I will identify what JDOM-specific pointers or handlers exist for string extraction.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
